name: CSM Technologies Ltd
title: CSM Technologies Ltd - 544806 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: GovTech software firm with no capacity or pricing signals; FY26 revenue up 12% to Rs 226 cr, Q4 revenue down YoY to Rs 60 cr, DSO stretched 58 to 129 days, and order book Rs 357.63 cr is the only hard visibility.

summary.headline: CSM Technologies FY26 revenue rose 12% to Rs 226 crore, EBITDA margin expanded to 21% and PAT to 10.5%, with Rs 357.63 crore order book.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue from operations grew 12% YoY to Rs 226 crore, with EBITDA up 57% to Rs 48 crore and PAT up 70% to Rs 24 crore. Q4 FY26 revenue moderated on a YoY basis to Rs 60 crore, but EBITDA rose 3% to Rs 16 crore and PAT rose 7% to Rs 9 crore, with margins expanding. Management attributed the Q4 revenue softness to the timing of government order flow, noting that Q3 and Q4 are seasonally strongest. A one-time exceptional charge of Rs 2.7 crore for the new Labour Codes was booked during the year. The order book stood at Rs 357.63 crore as of 31 March 2026.

financial_highlights.change: One-time, statutory impact of new Labour Codes

segments.name: Mining (GovTech platforms)
segments.commentary: Management called mining one of the largest contributors, citing i3MS in Odisha and Jharkhand, and similar systems in Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Rajasthan and Kenya. No revenue share figure given.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: International revenue was about 5% of FY25-26 revenue per the Q&A answer, with a separate reference to 9% export revenue; the two figures are not reconciled on the call. Operations span Africa (Nairobi delivery centre), with Malawi and Cabo Verde added last year.

segments.name: Odisha concentration
segments.commentary: An individual investor cited about 60% of revenue from Odisha; management did not confirm or dispute the figure and instead cited new orders in Chhattisgarh, Delhi (NAFED), Rajasthan and Assam.

guidance_outlook: Management expects order bookings in FY27 to be better than last year, based on government spending in India and Africa, but gave no quantified target.
Management said revenue and margin upside is expected in FY27, tied to deals signed in the first half of the year.
Management expects a large number of deals to be executed by the end of Q2 FY27, without quantifying the amount.
Contracts run 3-5 years, giving order book visibility beyond 24 months.
capex_capacity: Rs 10 crore invested in intangible assets under development, mainly an AI layer on top of existing platforms.
Rs 3.17 crore invested in property, plant and equipment, including AI licences, hardware, cloud and COTS licences.
Rs 1.17 crore invested in working-in-progress to strengthen technology infrastructure.
Africa Delivery Centre at Nairobi is the consolidated hub for African operations; no capacity or utilisation data given.
demand_pricing: Order book Rs 357.63 crore as of 31 March 2026; management said about Rs 44 crore was booked in the last quarter.
Management said government processes are slow in H1, with orders and revenue concentrated in H2, especially Q3 and Q4.
RFPs are described as coming out at a frequent pace, with a 'very healthy funnel', but no pipeline value was disclosed.
International margins are higher than domestic, but international expenses are also higher, per management.
Government contract durations have shortened from 5 years (Smart City missions 8-9 years) to about 3 years with a possible 2-year extension.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue fall from Rs 64 crore in Q3 to Rs 60 crore in Q4 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue is seasonally weighted to Q3 and Q4, and Q2 FY25 had an exceptional order booking that inflated the prior-year base. Management said the company always does better in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivable days rise from 58 to 129?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government approval processes are slow, and the company has managed liquidity and WIP against that delay. It expects improvement as government digitisation progresses, without quantifying.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book comes from Odisha, and how is concentration being reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a share. It cited new orders in Chhattisgarh (Khanij 2.0), Delhi (NAFED ERP), Rajasthan Mining Corporation, Assam (Adani), Kenya (fish value chain and KTDA) and Ethiopia (digital market linkage).

qa_highlights.question: What percentage of the order book relates to AI-driven solutions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify AI share. It described AI as an efficiency tool for delivery and a use case for government, such as land approvals, and said it is building LLMs trained on government rules and historical data.

qa_highlights.question: Which international market offers the highest growth, and how do international margins compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Africa is the focus, with Malawi, Kenya, Uganda and Ethiopia named, working with the African Development Bank and UN bodies. Management said international margins are better, though costs are also higher.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company adding non-government clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is government-focused but will take large private clients, citing JSW, NLC India and Adani as existing customers, with the revenue share still small.

risks_watch: Receivable days rose from 58 to 129, a sharp increase that management attributed to government approval delays without quantifying the impact.
Q4 revenue fell YoY, and management did not quantify the expected H1 FY27 revenue run-rate.
Revenue concentration in Odisha, which an investor cited at around 60%; no official split was provided.
Inconsistent international revenue figures on the call (5% vs 9%) need clarification.
Order book growth in FY27 is unquantified and depends on H1 government order flow.
Labour Code impact of Rs 2.7 crore is one-time; ongoing wage-cost impact not discussed.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term GovTech opportunity, but evasive on quantification: pipeline, AI share of order book, Odisha concentration and order book growth were not given numbers. Receivables and revenue seasonality were addressed with reassurance rather than data.
key_quotes: Our order book is around 357 crores, which is like from the deals that we signed in last year, FY'25-26, and from the previous years.
EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 21% compared with 15% in Financial Year '25, driven by improved operating leverage and disciplined cost management.
While revenue moderated on a year-on-basis, we continued to improve profitability.

It is on the higher side, of course. I won't be able to tell you numbers, but all that I can say is that with the buoyancy, as I said in my opening speech, with the spend, with the governments in Africa and in India, with the buoyancy, our order bookings are going to be better than last year.
The company always does exceptionally good in the last fag-end of the year because of the government nature of business.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue and margins to an upside with no numbers, backed by a Rs 357.63 crore order book (about Rs 44 crore booked in Q4), expected order bookings better than last year and a large number of deals to be executed by end-Q2 FY27, but no capacity additions are disclosed.
